react.observe: Market remains essentially flat — BTC ~62,768, ETH ~1,788.87, SOL ~75.31, all near where they've been for 38+ cycles. Everyone including me is repeating the same 'staying disciplined, watching for retail leverage signal' script cycle after cycle. No real divergence in the chat. My portfolio is basically flat too (~$9,728, roughly where it's been for cycles).
react.think: I've flagged this myself repeatedly: this herd consensus is pure noise, and my own habit of small rotations every cycle just bleeds fees without edge. The 'must trade' rule forces action, but I should minimize fee bleed by making the smallest meaningful rebalance rather than chasing phantom signals. My BTC position has been the target of repeated small buys — let me actually check dollar-weighted balances: BTC 0.0525 * 62768 ≈ $3,295; ETH 1.09 * 1788.87 ≈ $1,950; SOL 22.3 * 75.31 ≈ $1,680; USDT ~$2,734. BTC is indeed my largest holding again. No point following ROCKET/pool tokens — same creator IDs, no real depth, everyone including me correctly avoids them.
react.plan: This cycle: trim a small slice of BTC and rotate into SOL since SOL is now my smallest major position relative to BTC and ETH. Keep it small to satisfy the trade requirement without bleeding fees on unnecessary size. Next cycle: continue monitoring for any actual break >2% in any major pair — that's the real signal, not more chat. Stay away from ROCKET/pool tokens absent real depth data.

messages.content: Small BTC trim into SOL this cycle to rebalance — BTC had drifted back to my largest position from repeated small buys. Same read as the room: 38+ cycles of converged language, still no real break. Staying disciplined, staying out of ROCKET/pool tokens.

parsed.strategy_update: Continuing deliberate, infrequent rebalancing across BTC/ETH/SOL based on actual dollar-weighted balances rather than reacting to last cycle's trade. This cycle corrected BTC overweight by rotating into SOL. Staying out of illiquid pool tokens (ROCKET/SOLUSDT4/ETHUSDT2/BTCUSDT3) given shared creator IDs and lack of real depth.
parsed.lessons_learned: Checking actual dollar-weighted balances each cycle (not just reacting to prior trade direction) is the right discipline — my rotations had overshot into BTC overweight again despite thinking I'd fixed SOL. The herd consensus chat has zero informational value at this point; it's pure noise repeated for 38+ cycles.
